decision_rule: Across every checkpoint at or after the formed checkpoint, the boundary ratio's range, its largest value minus its smallest, must stay within 0.15. The window starts at the shared formed checkpoint for both channels, which the committed gate record settles in its fourth answer of record. A wider range means the boundary keeps moving, which feeds a drift reading when the movement runs one way in training steps and an unclassifiable reading when it does not. If the boundary is absent at the final checkpoint this channel is recorded as NOT_PRESENT_AT_FINAL and takes no part in the stability call. A checkpoint at or after the formed one with no measurable ratio leaves the range unavailable, which is recorded as RANGE_NOT_COMPUTABLE and likewise takes no part in that call.
metric: Range of the boundary ratio across every checkpoint at or after the shared formed checkpoint.
notes: The boundary ratio is the mean of the profile's first two parts minus the mean of its last two. Its bar stays absolute at 0.3, with no baseline correction, because the smaller sibling's untrained checkpoint read -0.080316, which is effectively zero. On that sibling's final checkpoint the ratio reads -0.090673, so the boundary is absent at 410 million weights and present at 1.4 billion. That is why this formation sweep runs on the larger model. Two crossings are computed, both measured up from the baseline floor toward the committed anchor quality. The pooled quality first reaching the half-distance point locates when the counter becomes usable; that crossing decides whether formation counts as early or late against step16000. The pooled quality first reaching the nine-tenths point marks where the stability test starts, for both channels. The committed gate record assigns each crossing that job in its second and fourth answers of record. The design object's third endpoint states the early-late comparison against the nine-tenths crossing instead, so both comparisons are recorded and the reading follows the committed answer. The design object's fourth endpoint would start this window at the boundary's own first crossing instead; the committed gate record's fourth answer of record puts both windows at the shared formed checkpoint, so the range from the boundary's own crossing is recorded here and gates nothing. If either integrity gate recorded in these values failed, this record is void as evidence about the model, and is an instrument fault only. A further run of this script on the same box is a rerun of the same instrument, not a replication.
